reviewer: Codex relay account management implementation review
scope: Incremental relay/database source and complete owning-guide reconciliation; prior release reviews remain baseline for unchanged subsystem behavior.
decisions: Central-only retained lifecycle state; no second account registry or execution-project schema change.
Own-pool operator management, immutable audit, expected revisions, ticket invalidation and terminal account revocation.
Unknown evidence does not imply unhealthy account; stopped desktop does not imply failed registered account.
Consistent Primer-style management/removal and Cloudscape icon-plus-text status within existing graphite/silver tokens.
ADR 0153 remains proposed; manual sign-ins, activation and provider qualification remain separate.
Whole owning guide updated for procedures, outcomes, recovery, installation and rollback; changed source paths map to relay/database with no unmapped source.
Bounded visual review inspected desktop/mobile rows and dialogs; final interaction rerun only for desktop denial. No new palette values or hook ignores.
findingsResolved: The first isolated SQL fixture exposed an enum-literal assumption; health mapping now compares text values and the full fixture passed.
Browser fixture now respects preserved disclosure state when opening Manage.
An extra HTTP fixture incorrectly treated permitted central scope fields as unknown; the unknown-field test uses a desktop ID, with peer denial covered in the database and monitor suites.
The read-only catalog check initially joined no pool identity; corrected to join the installation table. No mutation occurred.

Final review closed old direct-desktop controls and new display connections for removed registrations, and disconnects existing desktop sessions before stop. Rebuilt and reinstalled all affected images, reran browser interactions, HTTP/desktop tests and live acceptance.
Sandbox and local-tool access used scoped approved retries.
limits: No real provider account was registered; both pools have zero accounts, registration open and execution closed.
Provider sign-in, generation, physical phones, screen readers and streamed-desktop accessibility remain unqualified.
Health is derived from current metadata and confirmation, not an automatic provider test.
Removed accounts retain operational records and credentials; removal is not data erasure or remote provider session invalidation.
No execution-project migration, cloud service deployment or public application cutover.
The VMs remain on one trusted Mac and share its physical host and administrator.
